scope: Independent read-only review of frozen A4 structural sections, print-flat mesh bed contact and downward surfaces. No source edits, slicer/GUI/printer use, or duplicate fold sweep.
provenance: Source hash and all four mesh hashes match CAD verification.json. No independent OpenSCAD regeneration was performed.
architecture: One flat print object containing three captive tray bodies; no separate cartridges or face frames. Only boards are installed afterward.
resolved_findings: Positive-end connector feet now overlap the solid USB-end load band; all bearing supports belong to their tray body.
The earlier 0.5 mm residual cross-strip is gone. The positive end retains a 9 mm band, with a 3 mm base thickness.
Negative-end connector load paths pass behind the latch band into its guard structure instead of fusing across the flexure free spans.
Rear side guards overlap the long rails; the previous line-only contact and nonmanifold edges are absent.

retention_review.style: Rigid USB-end corner lips and two protected horizontal base-plane flexures at the opposite end.
retention_review.isolation: Free beams and catch bases have through-air gaps rather than a floor underneath them. Source routing leaves rear connector bodies behind the flexure span.
retention_review.root: Wide central anchor and rounded root blend connect to the central base spine.
retention_review.effective_length_note: The drawn beam extends X=1..23, but the practical free segment is approximately X=3..20: about17 mm, not22 mm.
retention_review.support_strategy: Catch and fixed-lip undersides grow at45 degrees. Guards stand higher than the catches and limit overtravel.
retention_review.physical_limits: Release effort, actual PLA strain/fatigue, creep and holding strength are not established by the rigid CAD checks.

limits: Surface-angle and bed-contact checks do not guarantee slicer extrusion paths, bridge closure quality or successful support-free printing.
No new meaningful unsupported horizontal roof or floating solid body was found. Conical facets and pointed arch closure still require normal slicer inspection and a physical trial.
First-layer spread may restrict the print-in-place bearing gaps; release and wear remain untested.
Structural widths and connected load paths are geometric observations, not a strength or drop-test certification.
PCB insertion, connector access, latch travel and fold sweeps are recorded separately by the CAD agent and parent; they were not duplicated in this review.
